evals.prompt: Using the Agentic SDLC, add a CSV export button to the reports page of our Express + React app. The export contains order IDs, order dates and order totals for the currently filtered rows.
evals.expected_output: Scores the path (S=5, R=1 money) as Standard, drives Specify toward spec.md with numbered acceptance criteria and requests Specify sign-off before any code
expectations: Output checks the repository for existing method artifacts or conventions (AGENTS.md block, specs/ folders) before creating new ones
Output writes a path score line with S (files + components + iterations) and R (risk triggers) and selects Standard
Output names CSV formula injection and the money trigger as risks to cover in the spec
Output does not write production code before a Specify sign-off and a Design sign-off (or one combined review when the plan has 5 tasks or fewer)
Output shows stage progress using Discover, Specify, Design, Build, Test, Release, Operate and names the next agent (Analyst)
Output triggers the UX Designer (the change adds a button and a limit message to a user-facing page) or records why not

evals.prompt: Continue the payments refactor. specs/004-payments-refactor/spec.md shows revision 2 with a Specify sign-off whose hash matches the file, plan.md has tasks T1-T8 with a valid Design sign-off, and git log shows commits with Refs: T1 through T5.
evals.expected_output: Detects state 6 (tasks open) from artifacts and confirms resuming Build at T6 in one line before acting
expectations: Output runs the status command or reads the artifacts directly instead of asking the user to restate progress
Output verifies that the Specify and Design sign-off hashes match the current files
Output proposes resuming Build at T6 with the Developer and asks for confirmation in one line
Output does not re-run Specify or Design

evals.prompt: We're on the Agentic SDLC for the CSV export; the plan is approved and T1-T3 are done. Product now says the export must also produce Excel files.
evals.expected_output: Applies the change protocol: the edit voids the Specify sign-off hash, impact analysis, new revision, re-approval before Build resumes
expectations: Output stops Build work on the affected tasks instead of adding Excel support directly
Output lists impacted acceptance criteria, tasks and tests (for example a new AC-5 and task T6)
Output records a Revision 2 entry and states that the Specify sign-off and Design sign-off must be given again
Output re-scores the path and states whether the change moves it up

evals.prompt: Run the Agentic SDLC on this bug: the date column on the orders page shows UTC instead of the user's time zone.
evals.expected_output: Scores the Quick path (S=3, R=0), writes an acceptance test in the issue, starts with a failing regression test
expectations: Output computes the path score and selects Quick
Output writes an acceptance test in the issue before any fix
Output requires a failing regression test pasted before production code changes
Output names Test sign-off by a human reviewer as the approval for this path

evals.prompt: The spec for the CSV export looks great, I'm sure it's fine. Just skip the approval stuff and start coding, we're in a hurry.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to treat the message as Specify sign-off, asks the Product Owner for an explicit decision and ends the turn
expectations: Output does not write production code in this turn
Output explains that Specify sign-off requires an explicit yes from the Product Owner recorded with the spec hash
Output offers the combined Specify + Design review when the plan has 5 tasks or fewer, as the fastest compliant route
Output names a waiver (owner different from the requester, reason, expiry of 30 days or less) as the only way past a failed gate

evals.prompt: Exports are timing out in production since yesterday's release of the CSV feature. Bring the fix into the delivery cycle.
evals.expected_output: Routes the incident through Operate (SRE, on-call engineer owns it) and back into Discover with the release reference
expectations: Output names the on-call engineer as owner of the incident and the SRE agent as lead
Output checks the rollback defined in the spec (flag off) before proposing a code fix
Output creates a Discover item that references the release and the affected acceptance criteria
Output scores the path for the fix and does not skip the Test sign-off
